'''Robert Endean''' (1925–1997) was an Australian marine scientist and academic at the [[University of Queensland]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.uq.edu.au/news/article/1997/10/respected-marine-scientist-dr-robert-endean-dies-after-heart-attack|title=Respected marine scientist Dr Robert Endean dies after heart attack|work=UQ News|access-date=2017-03-13|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Robert Endean was born in December 1925 in [[Abermain, New South Wales]], and was raised in [[Abernethy, New South Wales|Abernethy]]. He attended [[Cessnock High School]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cessnock.nsw.gov.au/community/events-ceremonies/halloffame/science|title=Hall of Fame – Science|publisher=Cessnock City Council|access-date=2017-03-13|archive-date=13 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313124837/https://www.cessnock.nsw.gov.au/community/events-ceremonies/halloffame/science|url-status=dead}}</ref> and won a scholarship to study at the [[University of Sydney]] taking a B.Sc. with Honours in zoology in 1948<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article193966596|title=26 Apr 1948 - "GO ALL OUT FOR AUTONOMY"|pages=5|via=Trove|access-date=2017-03-13|newspaper=Armidale Express and New England General Advertiser |date=1948-04-26}}</ref> and a University Gold Medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hawgood.co.uk/barbara/Endtalk2.rtf|title=ASPECTS OF THE WORK OF DR ROBERT ENDEAN (1925-1997): AUSTRALIAN MARINE BIOLOGIST AND TOXINOLOGIST|access-date=March 13, 2017}}</ref> He took his M.Sc from the same university in 1949, supervised by the marine biologist, Professor William Dakin. He took his PhD at the University of Queensland in 1958.

== Career ==
Endean worked as a secretary, and later chair and president, of the [[Great Barrier Reef]] Committee from 1954 to 1975. It was during this time that the [[Heron Island Research Station]] passed to the control of the University of Queensland. Endean took up work as an assistant lecturer in 1950, rising to the position of reader in 1964 at the University of Queensland.

Endean's primary research was the study of the toxicology of marine organisms.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article131723150|title=FLUORIDATION LAW EXPECTED SOON|pages=2|work=The Canberra Times|date=13 June 1963|via=Trove|access-date=2017-03-13}}<br>- {{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/08/04/science/jellyfish-s-fearsome-reputation-is-worse-than-its.html|title=Jellyfish's Fearsome Reputation Is Worse Than Its Sting|date=1981-08-04|work=The New York Times|author=John Noble Wilford|access-date=2017-03-13|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> particularly the crown-of-thorns starfish, [[Crown-of-thorns starfish|''acanthaster planc'']]<nowiki/>i.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article131670763|title=Saving a wonder of the world|date=1968-09-13|pages=2|via=Trove|access-date=2017-03-13|newspaper=The Canberra Times }}</ref> He became an advocate for the environmental protection of the reef,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://elibrary.gbrmpa.gov.au/jspui/bitstream/11017/2978/4/GBRMPA_2014_15%20AnnualReport_FINAL.pdf|title=Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority Annual Report 2014-2015|date=2015|access-date=March 13, 2017}}</ref> principally from the crown of thorns starfish,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article131685955|title=Barrier Reef being 'devoured'|pages=3|work=The Canberra Times|date=7 February 1970|via=Trove|access-date=2017-03-13}}</ref> and his publications and outreach work into the impacts of the starfish on coral ecology, led to the formation of the [[Great Barrier Reef Marine Park|Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority]] (GBRMPA) in 1975.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.oceanguard.com/the-team|title=Oceanguard – Save the Barrier Reef Now|website=Oceanguard – Save the Barrier Reef Now|access-date=2017-03-13}}</ref>

Endean accompanied [[Hans Hass]] on his first expedition to the Great Barrier Reef.<ref name=":1" /> In 1967, Endean accompanied the [[Belgian Scientific Expedition]] that conducted studies of the Great Barrier Reef.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://coralseaoz.blogspot.com/2012/07/birds.html|title=The Coral Sea (Australia): No.10 THE BELGIAN EXPEDITION (1967)|last=Harding|first=John H.|date=2012-07-06|website=The Coral Sea (Australia)|access-date=2018-06-25}}</ref>

In the 1960s, Endean worked with [[Hoffmann-La Roche|Roche Laboratories]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rae|first=Ian D.|date=2010-01-01|title=Marine Pharmacology in Australia. The Roche Research Institute at Dee Why, New South Wales, 1974-81|url=http://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=US201301853147|journal=Australian Journal of Chemistry|volume=63|issue=6|page=855|doi=10.1071/CH10073|issn=0004-9425|url-access=subscription}}</ref> to establish a research base at the Heron Island Research Station and study a number of active compounds found in marine organisms for medical research.<ref name=":0" /> He published 160 scientific papers and books during his career. His report prepared for the Queensland government into the outbreak of the crown of thorns starfish outbreak was dismissed in 1970.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thejohnharding3.wordpress.com/2005/08/31/crusader-of-the-reef-dr-robert-endean//|title=CRUSADER OF THE REEF ……. Dr Robert Endean|date=2005-08-31|website=John Harding|access-date=2026-01-24|archive-date=16 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216205609/https://thejohnharding3.wordpress.com/2005/08/31/crusader-of-the-reef-dr-robert-endean//|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref> A later report to the Commonwealth government was also tabled, for which Endean continued to provide research submissions.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.aph.gov.au/parliamentary_Business/Committees/House_of_Representatives_Committeesurl=reports/1985/1985_pp348.pdf|title=PROTECTION OF THE GREAT BARRIER REEF: Report of the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Environment and Conservation November 1985|publisher=Commonwealth of Australia|year=1985|isbn=0-644-04543-4|location=Canberra}}</ref>

Endean was a member of the [[World Health Organization|World Health Organisation]]'s Expert Advisory Committee on Food Additives. He was deputy chair of the Heron Island board which oversaw the research station. He was a spokesperson on reef ecology,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1988/0824/oreef.html|title=Starfish threaten Australia's Great Barrier Reef – and tourism. Scientists debate cause, remedy for outbreak of Crown of Thorns|last=Scott|first=David Clark|date=1988-08-24|work=Christian Science Monitor|access-date=2017-03-13|issn=0882-7729}}</ref> and had advised the community widely on toxins and marine pharmacology and biology.<ref name=":0" /> Endean retired from the University of Queensland in 1990, after 40 years of association with the Zoology Department.<ref name=":0" />

== Legacy ==
Endean died on 6 October 1997 on [[Heron Island (Queensland)|Heron Island]], shortly before he was due to give an address at the Australian Coral Reef Society. He was survived by his partner, Dr Ann Cameron, with whom he worked<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fairholme.qld.edu.au/news/view/206/leading-zoologist-leaves-lasting-impression|title=College News – Leading Zoologist Leaves Lasting Impression|publisher=Fairholme College Toowoomba|access-date=2017-03-13}}</ref> and daughter Dr Coralie Endean.

A reef was named for him – the Bob Endean Reef off [[Mission Beach, Queensland|Mission Beach]], Queensland.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.uq.edu.au/news/article/2015/02/reef-named-honour-of-uq-marine-advocate|title=Reef named in honour of UQ marine advocate|work=UQ News|access-date=2017-03-13}}</ref>
